variants.name: JPA AttributeConverter storing JSON (portable default)
variants.implementation_notes: The portable route uses the persistence provider's own extension point: an AttributeConverter implements convertToDatabaseColumn/convertToEntityAttribute once, @Convert (or autoApply = true) puts it on the entity attribute, and any JPA provider then maps the entity into a CLOB/TEXT or JSON column while the entity stays a plain POJO. Hibernate 6 absorbs even that step with @JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON) on the attribute, so the framework owns the JSON representation instead of converter code. Fields that must be queried, joined or indexed still belong in columns; the classic per-field mapping is the alternative once the entity is no longer read as a whole.
pitfalls: Converters must be null-safe, stateless and side-effect free: the provider may call them during dirty checks and result assembly, not only on save.
In-place mutation of a mutable payload can escape dirty checking - assign a fresh instance (or mark the attribute mutable) so the update is detected.
The converted column is opaque to JPQL and Criteria queries; anything you filter on must stay a mapped column.

variants.name: Serializable entity in a BLOB (classic J2EE realization)
variants.implementation_notes: The pattern's original realization (J2EE Design Patterns, carried by the java-design-patterns.com entry): the data object implements Serializable, the DAO writes it into a BLOB with ObjectOutputStream and restores it with ObjectInputStream, so no per-field mapping exists at all. Keep it for private, trusted, short-lived payloads only: the format is bound to the class's serialVersionUID and to Java's binary encoding, and deserializing database bytes instantiates whatever classes the stream names - a well-known attack surface.
pitfalls: Deserializing a stored stream runs readObject/constructors for the classes it names: never read payloads written by an untrusted writer.
Any change to the class's fields or serialVersionUID invalidates old rows (InvalidClassException) unless a serialization proxy or explicit versioning is designed in.
Lazy-loaded ORM proxies and session-bound collections are not persistable state - serialize plain data, not managed objects.
